name: axum (HttpArena axum entry)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', quictls TLS); h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma (C) and Drogon, userver, proxygen, agensio, cutelyst (C++) rows in the same suite
workload: HttpArena profiles for the axum 0.8 entry (hyper under axum, multi-threaded Tokio runtime, default configuration, tower-http gzip, serde_json): 16x pipelined HTTP/1.1 with 4096 connections, plus baseline-4096 (mixed GET/POST with query parsing), limited-conn-4096, json-tls-4096 and json-comp rows where it is slower.
claimed_speedup: pipelined-4096: 6,474,608 req/s vs nginx 4,037,345 (1.60x, derived from page data), h2o 4,938,603 (1.31x), agensio (C++) 4,958,241 (1.31x), proxygen 1,857,311 (3.49x), userver 1,395,512 (4.64x); but Drogon 7,801,404 (0.83x), cutelyst 10,167,331 (0.64x) and libreactorng 43,424,448 (0.15x) are ahead. Slower than the C servers on plain HTTP/1.1: baseline-4096 1,080,638 vs nginx 3,284,513 (0.33x), limited-conn-4096 685,038 vs 2,626,297 (0.26x), json-tls-4096 967,831 vs 1,313,755 (0.74x).
compiler_and_flags: axum: rust:1.94 image, cargo build --release with opt-level 3, codegen-units 1, lto thin, no target-cpu=native (frameworks/axum/Dockerfile and Cargo.toml). C side: nginx -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG (frameworks/nginx/Dockerfile); mongoose gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto.
hardware: HttpArena dedicated machine per site/data/current.json: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), CPU governor performance; each entry runs in a container. current.json is undated and may differ from the machine state of the run behind a given results file.
tradeoffs: Ergonomic router and extractor layer over hyper and Tokio; the layer adds allocation per request, which shows in the plain HTTP/1.1 rows.
caveats: HttpArena results JSON files are undated, hold one 5 s run per profile with no repeat count stated, and are rerun by the maintainers, so the numbers can move. The C and C++ competitor entries are minimal hand-written handlers (nginx with a custom C module, libreactorng, mongoose, h2o) built by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations. The nginx pipelined-4096 row (4.04M req/s) is far below libreactorng (43.4M), so every fast pipelined handler beats nginx there. axum runs on hyper, so this is the same engine as the hyper HttpArena record in the sibling w14-web-gh-cpp file and axum is the slower, higher-level wrapper (hyper baseline-4096 3,003,360 vs axum 1,080,638). The only clean win over C is the pipelined row, where the nginx number is the weak point; axum is behind nginx, h2o, mongoose and libreactorng on baseline-4096 and limited-conn-4096. The README itself only says performance is comparable to hyper and shows no numbers. Build flags: axum was not built with -march=native while the C entries were, which favours the C side.

name: Eclipse Vert.x (HttpArena vertx entry)

tradeoffs: JVM startup and warm-up, heavy memory (HttpArena shows 4.8 GiB on baseline-4096 and 16.9 GiB on async-32000 against 69 MiB to 3.5 GiB for the C entries on pipelined-4096), GC pauses; an event-loop model that must not block.
caveats: HttpArena results JSON files are undated, hold one 5 s run per profile with no repeat count stated, and are rerun by the maintainers, so the numbers can move. The C and C++ competitor entries are minimal hand-written handlers (nginx with a custom C module, libreactorng, mongoose, h2o) built by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations. The nginx pipelined-4096 row (4.04M req/s) is far below libreactorng (43.4M), so every fast pipelined handler beats nginx there. Vert.x wins over nginx and the C++ servers only on the pipelined row and the 32000-connection async row; it is 1.6x to 4.4x slower than nginx on the baseline, limited-conn and TLS rows. The repo README makes no numbers claim (it links BENCHMARKING.md, not opened). Memory use is an order of magnitude above the C servers. JIT warm-up inside a 5 s run is part of the number.

name: Robyn (HttpArena robyn entry)
baseline: nginx 1.31.4 (C, custom handler module, ./configure --with-cc-opt='-O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG', quictls TLS); h2o, mongoose, libreactorng, libioma (C) and Drogon, userver, proxygen, agensio, cutelyst (C++) rows in the same suite

Far behind on everything else: baseline-4096 430,749 vs nginx 3,284,513 (0.13x), limited-conn-4096 320,875 vs 2,626,297 (0.12x), latency-1m-1024 416,289 vs libreactorng 998,522 (0.42x).
compiler_and_flags: Not controlled: python:3.13-slim image, pip install of the prebuilt Robyn wheel (frameworks/robyn/Dockerfile), so the Rust compile flags of the runtime are unstated. C side: nginx -O3 -march=native -DNDEBUG.
hardware: HttpArena dedicated machine per site/data/current.json: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), CPU governor performance; each entry runs in a container. current.json is undated and may differ from the machine state of the run behind a given results file.
why_faster: None stated for the comparison; the README attributes Robyn's speed to its Rust runtime and multi-threaded design.
tradeoffs: Python handlers on a Rust HTTP runtime; the Python interpreter and GIL bound anything that runs per request in Python.
caveats: HttpArena results JSON files are undated, hold one 5 s run per profile with no repeat count stated, and are rerun by the maintainers, so the numbers can move. The C and C++ competitor entries are minimal hand-written handlers (nginx with a custom C module, libreactorng, mongoose, h2o) built by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations. The nginx pipelined-4096 row (4.04M req/s) is far below libreactorng (43.4M), so every fast pipelined handler beats nginx there. Tier B rather than A because the Robyn build flags come from a prebuilt wheel. The 4x pipelined win over nginx on a Python framework is implausible as a language or framework result: it more likely shows that the nginx handler's pipelined path is poor and that Robyn's runtime batches pipelined requests, since Robyn is 8x slower than nginx on the baseline row. Robyn's README claims 'Super Fast' and cites TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext but shows no numbers, and compares against Python frameworks rather than C servers.

name: tokio-websockets
baseline: mongoose (C, gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto, OpenSSL backend, epoll, one mg_mgr per core) and ringzero-ws (C, io_uring); proxygen (C++) rows in the same HttpArena suite
workload: HttpArena WebSocket echo profiles for a tokio-websockets 0.13 server on the multi-threaded Tokio runtime: echo-ws at 512, 4096 and 16384 connections, the rate-limited echo-ws-limited-512 and -4096 profiles, and 16x pipelined echo-ws-pipeline rows.
claimed_speedup: echo-ws-limited-4096: 2,641,801 msg/s vs mongoose 2,533,448 (1.04x, derived from page data), proxygen 1,063,324 (2.48x); echo-ws-limited-512: 2,171,052 vs mongoose 2,123,165 (1.02x). Unlimited echo-ws-512: 4,194,604 vs mongoose 3,954,919 (1.06x), echo-ws-4096: 4,198,339 vs 4,022,433 (1.04x), but ringzero-ws (C, io_uring) is ahead (4,353,147 and 4,429,548, so 0.96x and 0.95x). Pipelined rows lose: echo-ws-pipeline-4096 20,757,419 vs mongoose 59,017,072 (0.35x) and ringzero-ws 68,438,198 (0.30x).
compiler_and_flags: tokio-websockets: rust:1.95 with nightly-2026-06-27, RUSTFLAGS='-C target-cpu=native', opt-level 3, lto thin, codegen-units 1, panic abort, features sha1_smol, server and nightly (frameworks/tokio-websockets/Dockerfile and Cargo.toml). mongoose: gcc-14 -O3 -march=native -flto -std=gnu11.
hardware: HttpArena dedicated machine per site/data/current.json: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3995WX 64-Cores (64 cores, 128 threads), 251 GiB RAM, Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-22-generic, Docker 29.3.0 (runc), CPU governor performance; each entry runs in a container. current.json is undated and may differ from the machine state of the run behind a given results file.
tradeoffs: Strict RFC 6455 compliance (UTF-8 and close handshake validation), which the repo's own benches README contrasts with non-strict libraries; the HttpArena build enables the crate's nightly feature.
caveats: HttpArena results JSON files are undated, hold one 5 s run per profile with no repeat count stated, and are rerun by the maintainers, so the numbers can move. The C and C++ competitor entries are minimal hand-written handlers (nginx with a custom C module, libreactorng, mongoose, h2o) built by the suite maintainers or contributors, not tuned production configurations. The margin over mongoose is 2 to 6 percent, within plausible run-to-run noise for a single 5 s run, and the faster C entry (ringzero-ws) beats it on the unlimited rows and by 3x on the pipelined rows. mongoose is a general embedded networking library, not the fastest C WebSocket server; uWebSockets is absent from the suite. The nightly toolchain and target-cpu=native were used for the Rust side. The project's own benches/README.md uses uWebSockets (C++) as a reference with chart images only (not read for numbers).

name: Caddy
workload: HTTPS reverse proxying, per the title of a blog post discussed on Hacker News; the post itself was not opened. An independent two-scenario repo (hello-docker 'hello world' response and a 256K file, Vegeta at 500 req/s for 10 s) and the HttpArena suite were opened as cross-checks.
claimed_speedup: 'Caddy Outperforms Nginx 4x' (title of the HN submission 'HTTPS Reverse Proxy: Caddy Outperforms Nginx 4x', item 33725154; snippet only, number not verified). Cross-checks do not support it: github.com/patrickdappollonio/nginx-vs-caddy-benchmark shows nginx faster on the hello response (mean 337.36 us vs Caddy 385.502 us) and Caddy faster on a 256K file in the first run (mean 1.310211 ms vs nginx 1.536594 ms, 1.17x derived from page data) but nginx faster after a later commit (1.192198 ms vs 1.471049 ms).
compiler_and_flags: Docker compose images; versions and build flags not stated on the page.
hardware: Laptop, Intel Core i7-10710U 6 cores, about 15.7 GB RAM, Pop!_OS 22.04 LTS, kernel 6.0.6 (from the benchmark README).
tradeoffs: Automatic HTTPS and a Go module system; higher CPU and memory per request than nginx; garbage-collected runtime.
caveats: Recorded as a contradicted claim. HttpArena (public code, A-grade suite) shows Caddy 4 to 17x slower than nginx on every shared row: baseline-4096 431,894 vs 3,284,513 req/s (0.13x), limited-conn-4096 237,689 vs 2,626,297 (0.09x), pipelined-4096 761,137 vs 4,037,345 (0.19x), json-tls-4096 321,964 vs 1,313,755 (0.25x), static-tls-1024 159,177 vs 720,869 (0.22x), baseline-h3-64 360,511 vs 4,849,624 (0.07x), at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MDA2AV/HttpArena/HEAD/site/data/results/caddy.json (Caddy with custom Go handler modules versus nginx with a custom C module compiled -O3 -march=native). The 4x figure could not be traced to a page that was opened (blogs blocked); the Caddy README makes no performance claim. Tier C at most; arguably not faster.
